title: The Protocol of Sector Nine Anew
premise: Beatrix Crane smuggles memories in sealed neural vials past orbital customs, funding her lonely vigil over a beacon that predates all records. When the ship Halcyon returns from deep space with its crew aged backward into childhood, Beatrix discovers the beacon she tends is a countdown tied to a fleet-wide cryosleep truce — one half of humanity must wake first, and the other half stays frozen. As customs agents, memory cartels, and the child-crew of the Halcyon converge on Sector Nine, Beatrix realizes the beacon was built by her own forgotten self, and that the memories she smuggles include her own erased past. In the end, she chooses to wake the children's generation first, sacrifices her contraband fortune to broadcast the truth, and accepts that the woman she was is gone — but the family she's found is not.
about_author: Freya Almeida is a former radio astronomer who left observatory life to write fiction about the signals we refuse to hear. She lives aboard a converted ferry with her partner and an unreasonable number of houseplants.

chapters.title: Contraband and Starlight
chapters.summary: Beatrix runs a memory shipment past orbital customs using a smuggler's blind spot she's used for years, then returns to tend the ancient beacon she alone maintains. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: competent loneliness, the comfort of routine hiding a hollow core.

chapters.title: The Ship That Sailed Backward
chapters.summary: The Halcyon limps into dock, its forty crew members transformed into children under ten, memories intact but bodies decades younger. Customs seals the ship; Beatrix, bribed to retrieve one vial from the wreck, glimpses a child officer who calls her by name. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: uncanny dread.

chapters.title: Vials of Yesterday
chapters.summary: Beatrix examines the vial she stole: it contains a memory of the beacon's construction, filmed from inside her own skull. She confronts her fence, Odile, who admits the memory trade in Sector Nine traces back to a single source — the Halcyon's original mission. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: vertigo of self-doubt.

chapters.title: Children of the Deep
chapters.summary: Beatrix smuggles herself aboard the quarantined Halcyon and meets the child-crew, led by ten-year-old Captain Ilsa Reyes, who remembers commanding a ship she can no longer reach the controls of. Ilsa offers alliance: her crew's adult memories hold the truce's terms. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: reluctant tenderness.

chapters.title: The Truce Clock
chapters.summary: Ilsa explains the fleet's founding bargain: two cryosleep arks, one per faction, and a beacon-timed truce deciding who wakes first. The beacon Beatrix maintains is that timer — and it's accelerating. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: the weight of adult duty in a child's hands.

chapters.title: Customs Comes Calling
chapters.summary: Inspector Davor Kell, hunting the memory smuggler 'Wren,' narrows in on Beatrix while secretly harboring his own purchased memories of a daughter he lost. He raids Odile's shop; Odile burns her ledger and names Beatrix under duress. POV: Kell. Emotional beat: duty grinding against grief.

chapters.title: What the Beacon Remembers
chapters.summary: Beatrix decodes the beacon's maintenance logs and finds her own handwriting from decades she cannot recall — she has reset her memory before, more than once. The vial memory shows her volunteering for the erasure. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: horror and strange pride entwined.

chapters.title: The Cartel's Price
chapters.summary: The Meridian cartel, which controls the memory trade, offers Beatrix a fortune to let the beacon run its course — their fortunes depend on the current waking order. She refuses; they seize Odile as leverage. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: the cost of conscience.

chapters.title: Small Hands, Heavy Keys
chapters.summary: The child-crew votes to help Beatrix reach the beacon's core, each contributing a fragment of remembered access codes. A quiet scene between Beatrix and young engineer Tam, who misses being forty, cements the found-family bond. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: grief for a self outgrown.

chapters.title: Kell's Bargain
chapters.summary: Kell corners Beatrix but hesitates when he realizes the Halcyon's children include the daughter whose memory he bought. He proposes an uneasy deal: her surrender in exchange for the children's immunity. POV: Kell. Emotional beat: a corrupt man choosing a first honest thing.

chapters.title: The First Erasure
chapters.summary: Beatrix recovers her oldest hidden vial and relives the night she first erased herself: she was the truce's original architect, and she buried the waking order because both factions cheated. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: meeting her former self as a stranger.

chapters.title: Siege at the Dock
chapters.summary: The cartel storms the quarantine ring to take the Halcyon's memory cores; the child-crew defends their ship with improvised traps while Beatrix and Kell hold the airlock. Odile is freed in the chaos but gravely injured. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: children forced to fight a war they inherited.

chapters.title: Half of Humanity
chapters.summary: With the beacon hours from triggering a default waking order, Beatrix lays out the choice: wake her faction first, or the children's. The child-crew, to her astonishment, votes to wake the frozen adults of the other faction — the generation that abandoned them. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: grace that outstrips age.

chapters.title: Odile's Ledger
chapters.summary: A dying Odile gives Beatrix the ledger's true final page: a list of every memory the cartel bought from the beacon's original builders — including the second half of Beatrix's erased confession. POV: Kell. Emotional beat: a legacy passed in a whisper.

chapters.title: The Second Confession
chapters.summary: The recovered memory reveals the waking order was never a countdown but a choice-point: the beacon's true function is to ask, not to decide. Beatrix realizes her past self left the decision deliberately unmade — for her future self to make freely. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: forgiveness of the self she was.

chapters.title: Everything Wren Owed
chapters.summary: Kell arrests Beatrix publicly to satisfy his superiors while secretly clearing her path to the beacon core, burning his own career. Their goodbye on the transport is clipped, mutual, and final. POV: Kell. Emotional beat: sacrifice disguised as betrayal.

chapters.title: The Core
chapters.summary: Beatrix, Ilsa, and Tam breach the beacon's core chamber and find the interface keyed to a living mind — it will accept only the architect's, meaning hers. The beacon begins its default sequence; minutes remain. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: terror at the threshold.

chapters.title: The Question the Beacon Asks
chapters.summary: Clamped into the interface, Beatrix faces the choice her past self deferred: who wakes first. Remembering the child-crew's vote, she chooses the frozen strangers of the other faction — mercy over faction, strangers over kin. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: the climax of self-authorship.

chapters.title: Waking
chapters.summary: Across the system, cryopods open; the first woken adults emerge confused into a station guarded by children and a smuggler. Among them is the man from Beatrix's oldest memory — the person she erased herself to protect. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: dawn after a long night.

chapters.title: What the Cartel Cannot Buy
chapters.summary: The cartel collapses as the waking order becomes public knowledge; Beatrix broadcasts the beacon's true question to every settlement, making the choice permanent and communal. Kell, disgraced but free, chooses not to pursue her. POV: Kell. Emotional beat: truth as the only unstealable currency.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Was Wren
chapters.summary: Beatrix chooses not to restore her erased memories, keeping only the vial as a sealed letter to herself. She and the child-crew refit the Halcyon as a ferry between the waking factions. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: peace with an unfinished self.

chapters.title: Sector Nine, Anew
chapters.summary: One year later, the beacon no longer counts down; it broadcasts the question — who wakes next? — and waits for an answer given freely each cycle. Beatrix, Ilsa, and Tam light it together. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: found family under a signal that finally means hope.
